seo.meta_description: Toyota C-HR 2016-2023 import NZ via Japanese auctions. Compare NGX10, NGX50 and ZYX11 codes before bidding.
seo.og_title: Toyota C-HR 2016-2023 Japan import to NZ
seo.og_description: Import a Toyota C-HR from Japan with guidance on NGX10, NGX50 and ZYX11 body codes, hybrid options, auction information and landed-cost estimates.

blocks.hero_subtitle: The C-HR is Toyota’s coupe-styled compact SUV, and the 2016-2023 import search splits into three useful codes: NGX10 front-drive 1.2 turbo, NGX50 4WD 1.2 turbo and ZYX11 1.8 hybrid. We confirm the exact code, grade, transmission, listed equipment and import viability before any bid is placed.
proof_points: Japan auction access with model-code guidance
Importing Estimate - compliance is part of the process
blocks.why_kiwis_buy: Buyers look at the C-HR because it is easier to park than a larger SUV while still giving five doors and five seats. The ZYX11 hybrid has a listed 25.8 km/L WLTC figure on the G Mode-Nero Safety Plus III, while the NGX50 gives 4WD for buyers who prefer the petrol turbo layout.
blocks.video_caption: A walkaround is useful on a C-HR because the rear door shape, boot opening and cabin layout matter more than they do on a boxier SUV. We match what is visible against the auction list before you decide on a bid.
blocks.main_usp_deep: The useful part of importing a C-HR from Japan is choice. The search can target the ZYX11 hybrid for economy, the NGX50 4WD turbo for all-weather traction, or the NGX10 2WD turbo where price and transmission choice matter. Toyota's 2019 C-HR minor-change release states Display Audio and DCM became standard across the C-HR range, while some parking-support systems remained grade or option dependent.

buyer_persona.headline: Is this car right for you?
buyer_persona.body: The C-HR suits someone who wants Toyota hybrid efficiency or a compact SUV with a bit more shape than a boxy hatch. It is not the roomiest Toyota SUV, so buyers carrying bulky prams or tall rear-seat passengers should compare it with Corolla Cross before bidding. For commuting, parking and weekend use, the ZYX11 hybrid is the economy-focused option.

car_specs_benefits.spec: ZYX11 THS II 1.8L hybrid with 2ZR-FXE engine and FF
car_specs_benefits.benefit: The version to target when the priority is low fuel use rather than 4WD.

car_specs_benefits.spec: ZYX11 G Mode-Nero Safety Plus III WLTC 25.8 km/L
car_specs_benefits.benefit: That converts to about 3.9L/100km, a useful figure for daily commuting and town driving.
The 4WD turbo version suits buyers who want the C-HR shape without choosing the hybrid drivetrain.

car_specs_benefits.spec: NGX10 8NR-FTS 1.2L turbo, FF, Super CVT-i or 6-speed iMT after the 2019 minor change
car_specs_benefits.benefit: The 2WD turbo can suit buyers comparing purchase price and transmission preference.

car_specs_benefits.spec: Five doors, five seats, 4385mm length and 1795mm width on post-2019 catalogue examples
car_specs_benefits.benefit: Compact enough for city parking, with a wider stance than a small hatch.

standout_features_block.headline: The clever bits
standout_features_block.intro: C-HR equipment changes by body code, year and grade, so these items need to be confirmed on the exact auction car.

items.title: Toyota Safety Sense
items.body: Toyota's 2022 C-HR equipment table shows Toyota Safety Sense as standard on the grades in that table, with Pre-Collision Safety including daytime and night-time pedestrian detection, daytime cyclist detection, Lane Tracing Assist, Automatic High Beam and all-speed Radar Cruise Control. We confirm whether the exact auction car carries the listed suite before bidding.
items.image_hint: Dashboard view showing Toyota driver-assist indicators active ahead of a marked lane

items.title: Display Audio and DCM from the 2019 minor change
items.body: From the 2019 minor change, Display Audio and DCM are listed across the C-HR range. This is a useful dividing line when comparing an earlier car with a later NGX10, NGX50 or ZYX11.
items.image_hint: Interior dashboard photo focused on the factory central display screen

items.title: Parking-support equipment on selected grades
items.body: Intelligent Clearance Sonar, Parking Support Brake, Panoramic View Monitor and Rear Cross Traffic Auto Brake are listed as optional or special-grade equipment depending on year and grade. Mode-Nero Safety Plus versions are worth checking closely because some of this parking equipment is specifically listed there.
items.image_hint: Centre screen showing a 360-degree parking camera view beside a kerb

items.title: GR Sport grades
items.body: S-T GR Sport appears in NGX10 and NGX50 1.2 turbo form, while S GR Sport appears in ZYX11 hybrid form. The badge changes the buying brief, so we confirm the exact grade and drivetrain before any comparison is made.
items.image_hint: Close view of GR Sport seat and steering-wheel details inside the cabin

tech_deep_dive_block.headline: Under the skin
tech_deep_dive_block.intro: The C-HR is simple to understand once the body code is confirmed, because each requested code points to a different drivetrain path.

items.title: ZYX11 Toyota Hybrid System II
items.body: ZYX11 is the C-HR hybrid code in this search. It uses Toyota’s THS II system with the 2ZR-FXE 1.8-litre engine and an electric continuously variable transmission driving the front wheels. It is a self-charging hybrid, so there is no charging cable or plug-in routine. Around town, the system can move between electric assistance and petrol power without the driver managing modes.

items.title: NGX10 and NGX50 8NR-FTS turbo
items.body: NGX10 and NGX50 use Toyota’s 8NR-FTS 1.2-litre turbo petrol engine, with Toyota's C-HR catalogue data listing output at 85kW. NGX10 is the front-drive version, while NGX50 is the 4WD version with Super CVT-i. After the 2019 minor change, NGX10 petrol grades include both Super CVT-i and 6-speed iMT options depending on grade. This is why the transmission has to be confirmed from the exact auction list before pricing two cars against each other.

items.title: 2016-2023 C-HR size and body layout
items.body: The 2016-2023 C-HR import search covers NGX10, NGX50 and ZYX11, with NGX10 added from 2018 and the ZYX11 hybrid appearing after the 2019 minor change. Catalogue examples for post-2019 NGX10 and ZYX11 list a five-door, five-seat body at 4385mm long, 1795mm wide and 1550mm high. NGX50 examples are listed at 1565mm high, which reflects the 4WD packaging. The wheelbase listed for the ZYX11 G Mode-Nero Safety Plus III is 2640mm, so it sits in the compact SUV class rather than the larger family-SUV space.

models_comparison.intro: Use the body code first, then compare grade and equipment.

rows.notes: Checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding; final certification occurs in NZ.

NGX10: 8NR-FTS 1.2 turbo, 85kW, FF, Super CVT-i or 6-speed iMT by year and grade. NGX50: 8NR-FTS 1.2 turbo, 85kW, 4WD, Super CVT-i. ZYX11: 2ZR-FXE 1.8 hybrid with THS II, FF, electric continuously variable transmission.

S-T is the entry turbo path, G-T adds higher-grade turbo positioning, G is the main hybrid grade, Mode-Nero Safety Plus III adds special-edition equipment, and GR Sport targets buyers wanting the sport-themed grade.
Current availability and pricing need to be checked against live auction data before any bid limit is recommended.

faq_block.q: Which Toyota C-HR code should I look for?
faq_block.a: Choose ZYX11 if you want the 1.8 hybrid. Choose NGX50 if you want the 1.2 turbo with 4WD. Choose NGX10 if you want the 1.2 turbo front-drive version, including the later iMT option on some cars.

faq_block.q: How is the Importing Estimate handled?
faq_block.a: We prepare the Importing Estimate against current auction information and the exact vehicle being considered. Compliance and on-road costs remain variable until checked for that vehicle.

faq_block.q: Can you confirm compliance before I bid?
faq_block.a: Import viability must be checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding; final certification occurs in NZ. We support the process, but the final outcome cannot be promised before NZ certification.

faq_block.q: How long does a C-HR import take?
faq_block.a: Timing depends on auction success, Japan-side processing, shipping, customs clearance and NZ arrival steps. We give updates as the process moves forward rather than promising a fixed arrival date before the car is bought.

faq_block.q: What do you check on the auction list?
faq_block.a: We translate and explain the auction information available for the car, including grade, mileage, condition notes, damage markings, listed modifications and equipment notes when supplied. If information is missing or unclear, we say so.

not_for_you_block.headline: Who this may not suit
items: If you need maximum rear-seat access or a large boot opening, compare Corolla Cross before choosing a C-HR.
If you want 4WD and hybrid together, NGX10, NGX50 and ZYX11 do not provide that combination.
If you need a confirmed exact arrival date before purchase, importing is not the right process.

alternatives_block.intro: These are the closest researched alternatives to check before setting a C-HR bid limit.

rows.better_if: You want a similarly sized compact SUV with hybrid availability and a more conventional rear-door and cargo-area layout.
rows.tradeoff: Exact hybrid generation, drivetrain and Honda Sensing equipment change by year and grade, so each auction car still needs specification confirmation.

rows.better_if: You want a newer Toyota compact SUV option with hybrid availability and easier urban sizing than C-HR.
rows.tradeoff: It is smaller than C-HR, so rear-seat and luggage space will not suit the same buyer.

rows.better_if: You want a Toyota hybrid-capable SUV with a more practical, family-oriented body shape than C-HR.
rows.tradeoff: Compare current auction results and landed-cost estimates before setting the C-HR bid limit.

battery_health_block.headline: Hybrid battery information on exact cars
battery_health_block.body: The ZYX11 C-HR is a non-plug Toyota hybrid, so battery condition is not proven by the model code alone. If the auction list or supporting records include battery-related notes, we explain exactly what is supplied and what it does not prove.
checklist: Review any battery-related notes shown on the auction list
Confirm whether supporting records are supplied with the listing
Treat missing battery information as missing information, not as a positive claim

engine_drivetrain_block.headline: Powertrain options to confirm
engine_drivetrain_block.body: The 2016-2023 C-HR range is not one single mechanical specification. NGX10, NGX50 and ZYX11 need to be separated before price, economy and equipment are compared.
checklist: Confirm NGX10, NGX50 or ZYX11 on the exact auction car
Confirm CVT or 6-speed iMT on NGX10 petrol cars
Confirm FF or 4WD before comparing two turbo C-HRs
Confirm grade equipment from the exact listing, especially parking-support functions

savings_block.body: We calculate the estimate for the exact vehicle before you bid. It includes the vehicle cost, Japan-side costs, shipping costs, compliance, on-road costs and customs clearance. Compliance and on-road costs vary by vehicle, so they are confirmed in the current estimate rather than presented as fixed amounts.
